name: Minnesota
requirementsNote: Minnesota state law does not mandate renters insurance, but property managers frequently require proof of coverage in standard rental agreements.
seoDescription: Estimate renters insurance costs in Minnesota based on personal property, liability limits, and deductible options.

demographics.demographicNote: Most Minnesota renters choose thirty thousand dollars in personal property coverage with a five hundred dollar deductible, a level that fits the state's affordable overall rates while still accounting for genuine hail and winter storm risk.

riskFactors.title: Severe Hail
riskFactors.description: Minnesota ranks among the top five states nationally for hail damage, with sudden violent hailstorms common in late June and July capable of shattering windows and damaging siding in minutes. Hail damage to personal property is covered under a standard Minnesota renters insurance policy.

riskFactors.title: Extreme Cold and Ice Dams
riskFactors.description: Minnesota averages around one hundred seventy days a year below freezing, creating persistent risk of ice dams and frozen pipe bursts that can cause significant interior water damage. This type of sudden water damage is typically covered under a standard renters policy.

riskFactors.title: Spring River Flooding
riskFactors.description: Rivers including the Minnesota, Blue Earth, and Le Sueur face elevated flood risk during spring snowmelt and heavy summer rain. Flood damage from these rivers is excluded from standard renters insurance and requires a separate policy through the National Flood Insurance Program.

faqs.question: Is renters insurance required in Minnesota?
faqs.answer: No. Minnesota state law does not require tenants to carry renters insurance, though landlords are permitted to make it a condition of the lease.

faqs.question: Does renters insurance cover hail damage in Minnesota?
faqs.answer: Yes. Minnesota ranks among the top five states nationally for hail damage, and hail damage to personal belongings is covered under a standard renters policy.

faqs.question: Does renters insurance cover frozen pipe damage in Minnesota?
faqs.answer: Yes, in most cases. Sudden water damage from a burst pipe caused by Minnesota's extreme cold, which averages about one hundred seventy days below freezing a year, is typically covered under a standard renters policy.

faqs.question: Does renters insurance cover spring flooding in Minnesota?
faqs.answer: No. Flood damage from rivers like the Minnesota River during spring snowmelt is excluded from standard renters insurance. A separate flood policy through the National Flood Insurance Program is needed for that protection.

faqs.question: How much does renters insurance cost in Minnesota?
faqs.answer: Costs run at or near the national average, generally similar between the Twin Cities metro and outstate communities, though hail exposure runs higher in southern and western Minnesota. blogContent.whyThisRate: Minnesota renters insurance rates reflect a state defined by two extremes rather than one dominant hazard. Summer brings some of the most severe hail activity in the country, with Minnesota ranking among the top five states nationally for hail damage, particularly across the agricultural south and west. Winter flips the risk entirely, with the state averaging around one hundred seventy days below freezing a year and persistent ice dam and frozen pipe risk as a result. Spring adds a third, more localized layer, as rivers like the Minnesota and Blue Earth rise with snowmelt and heavy rain. Flood damage from that spring rise sits outside standard renters coverage, which limits how much of Minnesota's water related risk reaches the base rate compared to its hail and winter exposure.
blogContent.howCalculated: For a standard profile, twenty thousand dollars in personal property coverage, one hundred thousand dollars in liability, and a five hundred dollar deductible, our Minnesota renters insurance calculator applies the state's base rate of one hundred sixty five dollars a year with no adjustment at these default levels, landing around one hundred forty five to one hundred eighty five dollars a year, or roughly twelve to fifteen dollars a month. Renters comparing quotes in southern and western Minnesota with elevated hail exposure should expect real world premiums to run somewhat higher than this statewide baseline.
blogContent.comparisonNote: Within the Midwest region, Minnesota's rate sits close to Illinois and Indiana, sharing meaningful hail and severe storm exposure, though Minnesota's extreme cold and ice dam risk give it a distinct winter profile those states do not share to the same degree. Compared to the national average, Minnesota renters insurance runs close to typical levels, reflecting a state with real but balanced seasonal risk rather than one overwhelming hazard.
